description:
Blazing-fast Claude in your terminal — a C++26 alternative to claude-code.

agentty is a native C++26 terminal coding agent and a drop-in alternative to claude-code. A single static binary with sub-millisecond cold start, sandboxed by default, and one-command SSH air-gap. No Node, Python, or Electron. Signs in with your Claude Pro/Max subscription or an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Fixed
- Subagent reads no longer fail as not found on paths like
  main.go}},{. OpenAI-family models asked to batch reads sometimes
  wrote their internal multi-call wrapper
  ({"recipient_name":"functions.read","parameters":{…}}) inside one
  call's arguments, and a host that holds output to the tool schema turned
  it into path: "main.go}},{", symbol: "recipient_name". agentty ran
  that and the model only heard "not found". Now a single wrapped call to
  the right tool is unwrapped and runs. Anything else (several packed
  calls, a call to another tool, wrapper debris in a path or symbol) is
  refused as invalid arguments that tell the model to send each call
  separately. The check is in the one place every tool body runs, so it
  covers the main agent, subagents, ACP and mcp-serve alike. Subagent
  arguments that don't parse at all now fail as bad arguments (with the
  same hint when they are a wrapper) instead of running with {}.
- A leaked multi_tool_use.parallel call runs as the calls it holds.
  When that pseudo tool (or a tool_uses list under a real tool's name)
  reaches agentty, it is split at the stream into one real call per entry,
  for the main agent and subagents alike, instead of failing as "unknown
  tool". Ordinary calls are held only until their first argument key
  arrives. tool_args.wrapper_leak / tool_calls.parallel_fanout lines in
  agentty.log say when and with which arguments it happened.
- Project agents created mid-session are always seen. The agent
  discovery cache keyed on file mtimes only, so an agent file caught while
  still empty could be skipped for the whole process. It now keys on name,
  size and mtime.
Changed
- Built on the latest jaal, with the platform decided in one place.
  jaal now decides which OS, compiler and CPU agentty is being built for
  (jaal/meta/target.hpp), and agentty sees that only through maya
  (maya/core/target.hpp, the MAYA_OS_* and MAYA_CC_* macros). About
  550 checks of raw compiler macros (_WIN32, __APPLE__, _MSC_VER,
  __x86_64__, …) in agentty and maya were rewritten to those names. A
  script compiled every changed file for 15 targets (Linux, Android, macOS,
  the BSDs and Windows, on x86-64, arm64 and i386, with MSVC, clang-cl, GCC
  and clang) and confirmed the same code is chosen on each one. The build
  scripts ask the same headers too: cmake/AgenttyTarget.cmake instead of
  if(WIN32) / if(APPLE). New one_os and one_os_cmake tests keep it
  that way.
- Slow updates are logged with their message name. jaal's kernel times
  each update and reports the specific message type that ran over budget,
  e.g. loop.slow update msg::OpenPalette 23.1 ms. Before, agentty timed
  updates itself and logged a domain plus an index (ComposerMsg#7).
  Errors that jaal catches inside an update (an exception thrown while
  handling a message) are now written to agentty.log as loop.fault too.
  Before, they went only to stderr.log.
- Crash handlers use std::atomic_flag as the re-entry guard instead of
  volatile sig_atomic_t. It is just as signal-safe, it is also correct if
  two threads crash at once, and it passes jaal's concurrency checks.
- The activity bar explains what the stream is going through. Retries,
  stalls and slow starts are shown inline next to the phase indicator
  instead of in a banner that covered the bar:
  ⠋ retry 7s HTTP 503: service unavailable · 2/6 ━━━━━━━───.
  It shows the provider's reason and which attempt this is, and the bar runs
  down until the next try. After that it reads "… · trying again" and goes
  away at the first token. A stalled stream shows "no data for 47s ·
  reconnecting". A slow first token shows "waiting for the first token", or
  "the model is reading the prompt" on a local model. A working stream shows
  nothing extra; the token chart says enough. On a narrow terminal the token
  counts drop before the reason does.
- A message in the status bar no longer hides the gauges. Toasts used to
  take over the whole row, so the context and cache gauges disappeared for
  every "copied to clipboard" and for as long as any message stood. The
  message now sits on the left and the gauges stay on the right. On a
  terminal too narrow for both, the message wins.
- Retry countdowns update live. "retrying in 21s" counts down to the
  next attempt, then shows "retrying now" while it connects, instead of
  holding the first number for the whole wait. The phase chip counts down
  too ("retry 12s"), so the wait is visible even after the message fades.
- Banner colours match what happened. Rate-limit retries are amber,
  not the calm blue they had been painted (the line read "rate_limit —",
  and the colour check missed it; it now reads "rate limited —").
  "giving up after …", "could not …" and "… failed" are red.
Fixed
- Switching to a large thread is fast, and tmux no longer redraws the
  whole conversation. Opening a thread used to print its entire history
  into the terminal again, about 14 MB for a 2,200-message thread. That
  took 3 to 5 seconds and showed every row scrolling past in tmux. Now only
  the newest four screens are drawn, about 45 KB, and the thread is on
  screen about 30 ms after Enter. The ^J preview starts loading the moment
  the picker opens and settles 40 ms after you stop on a row (it was 90),
  and a thread file is parsed on all cores, about 85 ms for 16 MB instead
  of 280. The thread was also being read from disk twice: once for the ^J
  preview and again on open. It is now read once, reused if the file hasn't
  changed since the preview read it, and pressing Enter while the preview
  is still loading waits for it instead of starting a second read. Appearance ›
  Scrollback decides how much history is reprinted on open: on Auto (the
  default) none is, which makes switching instant; a fixed level (1k, 5k, 20k
  rows or the whole thread) reprints that much, which is slower on a big
  thread. Older
  messages are still in the conversation (^O) and in the file.
- The plan counter in the composer footer no longer jumps around while it
  updates. Each todo update rewrites the whole list, and the partly-sent
  list used to replace the plan every 120 ms. A plan at 3/5 showed 0/1,
  1/2, 2/3 and so on while the update arrived, and a finished step whose
  status hadn't arrived yet showed as undone. Now the items received so far
  are combined with the rest of the current plan, so the total stays put
  and a step's status changes as soon as it arrives. The exact new list
  takes over when the update finishes, before the tool has even run. An
  update that sends an empty list now clears the plan; before, it was
  ignored.
- A retry message can't outlive its turn. When the turn ends, any
  "retrying …" line goes with it. That includes "reasoning used the whole
  budget · retrying with less…", which nothing had ever cleared.
- "in progress" lines leave when the work does. "refreshing OAuth
  token…", "compacting context…", "rewinding to checkpoint…", "retrieving
  context…" and the self-update download line are now tied to the work they
  describe. Before, they cleared only on the success path, so a refresh that
  turned out not to be due left "refreshing OAuth token…" up all session.
- OpenCode Go and Zen show the cache in the status bar. OpenCode
  reports its cache only in its own usage.opencode.tokens (cache_read,
  cache_write_5m/1h), not in OpenAI's prompt_tokens_details, so agentty
  saw no cache at all and hid the CACHE gauge. It is read now.
- "retrying (upstream cut off)…" no longer sticks. On OpenAI-style
  providers (OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, custom hosts) one retried request left
  the banner up for the rest of the session, however well things went after.
  It now clears as soon as the retried stream produces anything, and lapses
  on its own after a few seconds regardless.
Full history: CHANGELOG.md
